chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from the one who asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I pray behind the one whom I do not follow with (i.e., a Non-Shia), so when I finish my recitation and he has not finished, he (peace be upon him) said: 'So glorify (with Tasbih) until he finishes.'

key_terms.أَقْتَدِي بِهِ: follow with (referring to school of thought/madhhab)

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I finish my Quran recitation during prayer behind a Non-Shia Imam who is still reciting?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of praying behind a Non-Shia Imam by focusing on the validity of the follower's individual actions rather than strict synchronization. It provides a practical legal solution for the 'follower's dilemma' when their recitation pace differs from the Imam's, instructing them to remain silent and engage in quiet glorification (Tasbih) until the Imam concludes his recitation. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the validity of the prayer is not invalidated by the Imam's potential minor errors or differing school practices, provided the follower performs their own obligations correctly.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,
(It has been narrated) from the one who asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I pray Salāt behind the one I do not follow with (Non-Shia), so then I tend to be free from my recitation and he is not free (from it)’. Heasws said: ‘So Glorify until he is free (from the recitation)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from the one who has asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said the following: I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can I perform Salah (prayer) behind one whom I do not follow and complete recitation when he has not yet completed?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Say Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects) until he completes.’”
